Head: 03ba18533d267b66d666bfedddb39771535e573d

No security vulnerabilities found in the reviewed changes. The repair addresses both prior telemetry notes:
- Retained seat-address keys are capped at 64 bytes; longer addresses count under "(other)". The existing fixed enum-key space and bounded seat-key count remain, so the prior large retained-address-byte caveat is closed for this projection.
- Arbitrary rejected-claim names are no longer retained. A refused name survives only when the refusal names that seat (retired/held), or the exact name registered successfully during this daemon run; other claims count under "(other)". The early route-refusal accounting respects that projection. No new registry read was introduced to justify retaining names.

Authenticated ping still exposes bounded legitimate/known seat identifiers and their historical tallies. This closes arbitrary rejected-name disclosure, not all identity visibility. No new sensitive ping fields or raw client attempt labels were introduced.

The route/service accounting, producer-label fixes and observer read-close lock introduce no new security finding in this delta. Correctness/performance own their accounting and late-observer closure verdicts; this security pass does not certify the whole issue or AC2's deferred live attribution.
